data.name: Aabad
data.gender_notes: Aabad is used as a male name in Persian and Urdu naming tradition.
data.long_meaning: Aabad (آباد) is a Persian name meaning “Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing”. It comes from Persian ābād (آباد) 'inhabited, cultivated, prosperous', itself from āb (آب) 'water'. It is not related to the Arabic ʿabd (عبد) 'servant', which is the separate name ʿĀbid / Abid. Ābād is a productive Persian and Urdu place-name element, seen in Islāmābād, Ḥaydarābād and Abbottābād.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabad carries the meaning “Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing”. Any spiritual reading placed on the name is interpretive and is labelled as such; the lexical meaning is the documented core.
data.etymology: From Persian ābād (آباد) 'inhabited, cultivated, prosperous', itself from āb (آب) 'water'. It is not related to the Arabic ʿabd (عبد) 'servant', which is the separate name ʿĀbid / Abid.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabad total 9, reducing to 9. Number 9 is associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aabad mean?
faq.a: Aabad means Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aabad?
What language does the name Aabad come from?
faq.a: Aabad is used in Persian, Urdu, Pashto and Hindi.

faq.q: Is Aabad a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabad is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Aabad written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aabad is written آباد in Arabic script.

faq.q: How is Aabad written in Urdu and Hindi?
faq.a: Aabad is written آباد in Urdu and आबाद in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aabad?
faq.a: The root of Aabad is Persian ābād (آباد), from āb (آب) water.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aabad?
faq.a: From Persian ābād (آباد) inhabited, cultivated, prosperous, itself from āb (آب) water. It is not related to the Arabic ʿabd (عبد) servant, which is the separate name ʿĀbid / Abid.

faq.q: Does Aabad appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabad is of Persian origin and is not a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is Aabad related to the Arabic name Abid?
faq.a: No. Aabad comes from Persian ābād, inhabited, cultivated. Abid (عابد) is a different Arabic name meaning worshipper, from the root ʿ-b-d. The two are unrelated despite the similar English spelling.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabad verified?
faq.a: Yes. The meaning Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing rests on the Persian/Urdu toponymic and personal-name element ābād, confirmed by Middle Persian ābād, populous, thriving, prosperous.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aabad?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabad total 9, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aabad?
faq.a: Variants and alternative transliterations include Abad and Aabaad.

faq.q: Where is the name Aabad used today?
faq.a: Aabad circulates chiefly in Persian, Urdu, Pashto and Hindi naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
